rows.description: A child whose parents respond only to marks feels loved for performance and hides mistakes; the harm is less the standard than the sense that love depends on meeting it.
The student erases and rewrites, avoids answering unless certain and feels sick over a small error. Every task now carries a threat to their worth, not just a chance to learn.
A child who stumbles while reading makes a silly face and gets the class laughing with them; the joke keeps control of the moment, though constant clowning can hide worry.

A teenager says "Great, just great" meaning the opposite, using tone or a flat delivery. Sarcasm can signal frustration, humour or contempt, and in text or across cultures it is easily misread, so a clarifying "Are you joking?" is fair.

rows.subtype: Friend all good then all bad [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager describes a friend as perfect one week and as a total traitor the next after a small slight; strong feelings make it hard to hold both good and disappointing sides together.

rows.subtype: Approach: negotiate shared costs with flatmates [Action]
rows.description: The employee proposes splitting groceries and internet with flatmates and buying staples in bulk from a wholesale market. Sharing costs stretches the same salary further without lowering quality of life.

rows.subtype: Feeling like a fraud in a top college [Actor]
rows.description: A student admitted to a prestigious institute believes they got in by luck and that everyone will soon find out; success is discounted while comparison with others is harsh.

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: When a task goes well, the person credits luck, the team or an easy assignment. Praise is filed away as a mistake in others' judgment, while any error is taken as proof.

rows.subtopic: Imposter feelings at a new job
rows.description: Confidence grows as competence does, and the person accepts that not knowing everything is normal. They begin to help the next newcomer, which cements their own sense of belonging.
